{{Short description|Psychometric response scale}}
[[File:مقياس_التناظر_البصري_(VAS)_لتقييم_إدراك_الألم_لدى_الأطفال.jpg | thumb | right | A visual scale used to assess pain intensity in children using numbers and graduated facial expressions]]
__TOC__The '''visual analogue scale''' ('''VAS''') is a [[psychometrics|psychometric]] response scale that can be used in [[questionnaire]]s. It is a measurement instrument for subjective characteristics or attitudes that cannot be directly measured. When responding to a VAS item, respondents specify their level of agreement to a statement by indicating a position along a continuous line between two end points.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Koo M, Yang SW|title=Visual Analogue Scale. |journal=Encyclopedia |date= Nov 2025 |volume=5 |issue= |pages=190 |pmid= |doi=10.3390/encyclopedia5040190|doi-broken-date=10 November 2025 |doi-access=free | url=https://www.mdpi.com/2673-8392/5/4/190/pdf?version=1762528583|hdl=1807/151010 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
==Comparison to other scales==
This continuous (or "analogue") aspect of the scale differentiates it from discrete scales such as the [[Likert scale]]. There is evidence showing that visual analogue scales have superior metrical characteristics than discrete scales, thus a wider range of statistical methods can be applied to the measurements.<ref name="Reips Funke">{{cite journal |last1=Reips |first1=U.-D. |last2=Funke |first2=F |title=Interval level measurement with visual analogue scales in Internet-based research: VAS Generator. |journal=Behavior Research Methods |volume=40 |pages=699–704 |year=2008 |issue=3 |doi=10.3758/BRM.40.3.699 |url=http://www.uni-konstanz.de/iscience/reips/pubs/papers/BRM2008reips&funke_interval_level_vas.pdf |pmid=18697664|doi-access=free }}</ref>

The VAS can be compared to other linear scales such as the [[Likert scale]] or [[Borg scale]]. The sensitivity and reproducibility of the results are broadly very similar, although the VAS may outperform the other scales in some cases.<ref name="Reips Funke"/><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Grant | first1 = S. | last2 = Aitchison | first2 = T. | last3 = Henderson | first3 = E. | last4 = Christie | first4 = J. | last5 = Zare | first5 = S. | last6 = McMurray | first6 = J. | last7 = Dargie | first7 = H. | year = 1999 | title = A comparison of the reproducibility and the sensitivity to change of visual analogue scales, Borg scales, and Likert scales in normal subjects during submaximal exercise | journal = Chest | volume = 116 | issue = 5| pages = 1208–17 | doi = 10.1378/chest.116.5.1208 | pmid=10559077}}</ref> These advantages extend to measurement instruments made up from combinations of visual analogue scales, such as semantic differentials.<ref name="Funke Reips">{{cite journal |last1=Funke |first1=F |last2=Reips |first2=U.-D. |title=Why semantic differentials in Web-based research should be made from visual analogue scales and not from 5-point scales. |journal=Field Methods |volume=24 |pages=310–327 |year=2012 |issue=3 |doi=10.1177/1525822X12444061 |s2cid=30305248 |url=http://www.uni-konstanz.de/iscience/reips/pubs/papers/Funke_&_Reips_(in_press)_%201.pdf }}</ref>

==Uses==
Recent advances in methodologies for Internet-based research<ref>U.-D. Reips (2006) Web-based methods. In M. Eid & E. Diener (Eds.), ''Handbook of multimethod measurement in psychology'' (pp. 73-85). Washington, DC: American Psychological Association. {{doi|10.1037/11383-006}}</ref> include the development and evaluation of visual analogue scales for use in Internet-based [[questionnaire]]s.<ref name="Reips Funke"/>

VAS is the most common [[pain scale]] for quantification of [[endometriosis]]-related pain and [[skin graft]] donor site-related pain.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Sinha S, Schreiner AJ, Biernaskie J, Nickerson D, Gabriel VA |title=Treating pain on skin graft donor sites: review and clinical recommendations. |journal=J Trauma Acute Care Surg |date=June 2017 |volume=83 |issue=5 |pages=954–964 |pmid=28598907 |doi=10.1097/TA.0000000000001615|s2cid=44520644 }}</ref> A review came to the conclusion that VAS and [[numerical rating scale]] (NRS) were the best adapted pain scales for pain measurement in endometriosis. For research purposes, and for more detailed pain measurement in clinical practice, the review suggested use of VAS or NRS for each type of typical pain related to endometriosis ([[dysmenorrhea]], deep [[dyspareunia]] and non-menstrual [[chronic pelvic pain]]), combined with the [[clinical global impression]] (CGI) and a [[quality of life]] scale.<ref name="BourdelAlves2014">{{cite journal|last1=Bourdel|first1=N.|last2=Alves|first2=J.|last3=Pickering|first3=G.|last4=Ramilo|first4=I.|last5=Roman|first5=H.|last6=Canis|first6=M.|title=Systematic review of endometriosis pain assessment: how to choose a scale?|journal=Human Reproduction Update|volume=21|issue=1|year=2014|pages=136–152|issn=1355-4786|doi=10.1093/humupd/dmu046|pmid=25180023|doi-access=free}}</ref>
VAS is being increasingly used for the assessment of loudness and annoyance of acute and chronic tinnitus.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Adamchic | first1 = I | last2 = Langguth | first2 = B | last3 = Hauptmann | first3 = C | last4 = Tass | first4 = PA | year = 2012 | title = Psychometric evaluation of visual analog scale for the assessment of chronic tinnitus | journal = American Journal of Audiology | volume = 21 | issue = 2 | pages = 215–225 | doi = 10.1044/1059-0889(2012/12-0010) | pmid = 22846637 }}</ref>

The usage of a visual analogue scale (VAS) measuring [[tokophobia|fear of birth]] (FOB) was first initiated by Rouhe et al.<ref name="Rouhe 67–73">{{Cite journal |last1=Rouhe |first1=H |last2=Salmela-Aro |first2=K |last3=Halmesmäki |first3=E |last4=Saisto |first4=T |date=January 2009 |title=Fear of childbirth according to parity, gestational age, and obstetric history |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1471-0528.2008.02002.x |journal=BJOG: An International Journal of Obstetrics & Gynaecology |language=en |volume=116 |issue=1 |pages=67–73 |doi=10.1111/j.1471-0528.2008.02002.x|pmid=19055652 |s2cid=40951634 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> FOBS is used to identify pregnant women with a fear of birth (FOB). It is a visual analogue scale (like VAS) that cover two constructs: worry and fear. The pregnant women are asked to rate their feelings about the approaching birth by responding to the question “How do you feel right now about the approaching birth?” on a paper with two 100&nbsp;mm VAS-scale printed on it. They indicate their feeling and respond by placing a mark on the lines with the anchor words “calm/worried” and “no fear/strong fear”. The two values on the VAS-scales are added up to give a total score ranging from 0 to 100.<ref name="Rouhe 67–73"/> Higher scores indicate higher levels of fear, and the cut-off point for fear of birth is 60.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hildingsson |first1=Ingegerd |last2=Rubertsson |first2=Christine |last3=Karlström |first3=Annika |last4=Haines |first4=Helen |date=October 2018 |title=Exploring the Fear of Birth Scale in a mixed population of women of childbearing age—A Swedish pilot study |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S1871519217302184 |journal=Women and Birth |language=en |volume=31 |issue=5 |pages=407–413 |doi=10.1016/j.wombi.2017.12.005|pmid=29249331 |s2cid=20377885 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>  Later on, FOBS, was then developed and tested based on Rouhe’s research in pregnant women in both Sweden and Australia.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ternström |first1=Elin |last2=Hildingsson |first2=Ingegerd |last3=Haines |first3=Helen |last4=Rubertsson |first4=Christine |date=April 2015 |title=Higher prevalence of childbirth related fear in foreign born pregnant women – Findings from a community sample in Sweden |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0266613814002939 |journal=Midwifery |language=en |volume=31 |issue=4 |pages=445–450 |doi=10.1016/j.midw.2014.11.011|pmid=25529841 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Haines |first1=Helen |last2=Pallant |first2=Julie F. |last3=Karlström |first3=Annika |last4=Hildingsson |first4=Ingegerd |date=August 2011 |title=Cross-cultural comparison of levels of childbirth-related fear in an Australian and Swedish sample |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0266613810000707 |journal=Midwifery |language=en |volume=27 |issue=4 |pages=560–567 |doi=10.1016/j.midw.2010.05.004|pmid=20598787 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> There have also been studies on pregnant women's thoughts when assessing fear of birth on the Fear of Birth Scale.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ternström |first1=Elin |last2=Hildingsson |first2=Ingegerd |last3=Haines |first3=Helen |last4=Rubertsson |first4=Christine |date=June 2016 |title=Pregnant women's thoughts when assessing fear of birth on the Fear of Birth Scale |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S1871519215003571 |journal=Women and Birth
